subject: general
question: What is the name of the southern half of the Pangaea supercontinent that existed about 300 million years ago?
solution:
The Correct answer is __**Gondwana**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Gondwana** was the name given to the **southern half** of the supercontinent **Pangaea**, which existed approximately **300 million years ago**.
 
• The term "Gondwana" is derived from the **Gondwana region in central India**, where some of the earliest geological studies were conducted.
 
• It included modern-day landmasses such as **South America, Africa, Antarctica, Australia, and the Indian subcontinent.**
 
• **Gondwana's breakup** began around **180 million years ago**, leading to the formation of the continents we see today.
 
• The geological evidence supporting the existence of Gondwana includes **similar fossil records**, such as the presence of **Glossopteris flora**, across these continents.
 
• Gondwana played a critical role in the study of **plate tectonics** and the understanding of continental drift.
 
• The fragmentation of Gondwana contributed to **major biodiversity changes** and the distribution of species across different continents.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Rodinia**__

 __
 
• **Rodinia** was a supercontinent that existed around **1.3 to 0.9 billion years ago**, much earlier than Gondwana.
 
• It is significant in the study of **Precambrian geology**.
 
• Rodinia eventually broke apart, leading to the formation of subsequent supercontinents, including **Pannotia** and later **Pangaea**.
 
 
 
• **Pannotia**__
 __
 
• **Pannotia** was a transient supercontinent that existed approximately **600 million years ago**.
 
• It formed after Rodinia but existed for a relatively short period before breaking into Gondwana and other land masses.
 
• Pannotia is less studied compared to Gondwana and Rodinia due to limited geological evidence.
 
 
 
• **Nuna**__
 
 
• **Nuna**, also known as the **Columbia supercontinent**, existed around **1.8 to 1.5 billion years ago**.
 
• It is one of the earliest known supercontinents and was significant in the **Proterozoic era**.
 
• Its breakup contributed to subsequent continental formations and the evolution of Earth's geology.
